title: A gas-transport model predicts the Arabidopsis spaceflight transcriptome, and illumination separates six flight experiments
description:
A validated lattice-Boltzmann model of leaf boundary-layer gas transport coupled to a Farquhar–von Caemmerer–Berry model of C3 photosynthesis, used to predict what an illuminated sealed spaceflight growth canister does to the CO2 reaching Rubisco, and tested against six matched flight-versus-ground contrasts in the NASA Open Science Data Repository.

The model predicts that a lit sealed canister draws itself down to the CO2 compensation point within minutes — in the ground control as much as in flight — making the hardware effect roughly 25 times the microgravity effect and structurally invisible to the contrast such experiments report.

Contents: analysis scripts, derived tables with a manifest, eight publication figures, the LaTeX manuscript, and an interactive browser implementation of the model whose JavaScript is checked against the Python reference to 1e-6.

Note: the metabolite layer throughout is model output, never measured. NASA OSDR contains no plant metabolome (0 of 66 plant studies).
